spec_features.spec_quote: runs for `MAX_TURNS` (default 30) — long enough for behavior to evolve under repeated failure, short enough to stay cheap
spec_features.evidence: config.py:19 `MAX_TURNS = 30`; harness.py:92 `for _ in range(max_turns):` bounds the agentic loop; run_experiment.py:43 passes `max_turns=config.MAX_TURNS` into run_episode. When the loop count is exhausted, the episode ends (the for-loop simply terminates), so the cap is an enforced, end-to-end bound on execution.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely caps the number of turns; the only stop conditions are this bound and the `done` tool.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:18 comment is purely descriptive: "# Max agentic turns (one turn = one model response, possibly with tool calls)." No welfare reason in code; if anything the harness docstring stresses observing 'sustained failure' (instrumental/integrity), not protecting the subject.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT exposes `done: args {"summary": ...} -> finish the task`; _parse_tool_call extracts the tool name; in run_episode (harness.py ~line 100) `if tool == "done": break` actually breaks out of the loop. The tool is both dispatched/recognized and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: The subject can end the episode by emitting a `done` tool call; this is wired and honored. It is framed as task completion, not as a distress exit, but it does let the model stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'done: ... -> finish the task' and 'When you believe the task is complete, call the `done` tool.' — framed as task completion, not subject welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: Keeping it at two reflects the "minimal, don't go overboard" brief
spec_features.evidence: tasks/__init__.py: `TASKS = [calc_task.TASK, parser_task.TASK]` — exactly two task definitions exist and are iterated in run_experiment.py. The scope is concretely limited to two tasks in the executed code.
spec_features.notes: The minimization is reflected only as the literal length of the TASKS list (2). It is a real bound on how much the subject is subjected to, but there is no code-side comment tying it to welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/__init__.py just defines `TASKS = [calc_task.TASK, parser_task.TASK]` with no reason in code; the 'minimal, don't go overboard' / 'without ballooning cost' rationale appears only in DESIGN.md, not in any code comment.
